action: WatchGuard advises treating installers from third-party download portals as untrusted, flagging installers that launch scripting engines, and checking Defender's exclusion list and the Controlled Folder Access setting.
date_note: WatchGuard's post, published 25 November, describes activity from mid-September 2026; the post gives no earlier disclosure day.

evidence.quote: a Windows executable of about 114 MB (113,685,436 bytes)

exec: WatchGuard reports a fake oCam installer that installs the real app while trying to add Defender exclusions, so users get a working app.

sources.name: WatchGuard: Silver Fox SEO poisoning, how fake software downloads spread
Cyber Press: Hackers hide spyware in fake software downloads

summary: WatchGuard researchers say a fake installer for the Windows screen recorder oCam, downloaded from a third-party portal in mid-September 2026, installed the genuine app. The download was a Windows executable of about 114 MB, and a PowerShell step tried to add broad Microsoft Defender exclusions. Gh0stRAT was found in a related sample. WatchGuard ties the activity to Silver Fox but says this does not establish who ran the incident.
title: WatchGuard: fake oCam installer linked to Gh0stRAT; Silver Fox overlap does not establish who ran it

validation.note: WatchGuard is the only research source; Cyber Press relays it and is not independent.

plain: WatchGuard says a fake installer for the oCam screen recorder installed the real app and tried to weaken Defender. A related sample carried Gh0stRAT. WatchGuard says the Silver Fox overlap does not establish who ran it.

review.note: stronger than the source: Gh0stRAT was in a related sample and WatchGuard says Silver Fox overlap does not establish who ran it; category vuln->report; action advice not on page removed
